title: Decouple the optimizer and explorer from specific data: no library items, runs, verdicts or dates in code
description: User (2026-09-27): 'Why would the docstring in any code need to refer to any specific data item in the database? Why would they be hard-coded and coupled like that?' Found: (1) comments and docstrings citing runs ('round 2/3'), dates, user decisions and verdict numbers (objective.py's WHOLE_MIX_MARGIN block cites run 2's A/B/C numbers; render_terms, archive, surrogate, cclicense, candidates, scripts/optimize.py); (2) real coupling in logic: scripts/optimize.py's positive controls hard-code specific clips (Funky Nurykabe sec-A1, an Ave hold) and a section fallback shaped like Ave House; audition_form's window default comment names Ave House. Fix: derive controls from the input score (the incumbent's own clip for its role; a silent control from any hold), derive fallback sections from the score's length, meter and structure; rewrite comments to say what and why only, pointing to where calibration lives (the verdict log, this task) without numbers or anecdotes. Keep behaviour and tests; add tests that the optimizer's controls and windows work on a score other than Ave House.
